spec.name: Spitfire Blueprint
spec.description: A Supermarine Spitfire Mk I at real size, built as a cyanotype blueprint: every surface is a flat Prussian blue, and panel seams, rivets, ribs and roundels are drawn on in white and pale cyan line-work.
spec.layout:
Single-engine low-wing monoplane, nose toward +Z, level attitude on two main wheels and a tail wheel, centred on x = 0. Extents: wingspan x = ±5.62, spinner tip z = +4.15, rudder trailing edge z = -4.97, propeller top y = 3.35. Only the main wheels and the tail wheel touch y = 0.

SHARED AIRFRAME FORMULAS (all parts must obey them so the pieces meet):
- Fuselage centreline height: y = 1.85 for z >= -0.9, falling linearly to y = 1.52 at z = -4.6. The propeller axis is y = 1.85, x = 0.
- Fuselage stations (z: centre y, half width, half height): 3.45: 1.85, .40, .40 | 2.9: 1.85, .45, .46 | 2.2: 1.85, .47, .50 | 1.9: 1.85, .46, .48 | 1.0: 1.85, .44, .52 | 0.2: 1.84, .43, .58 | -0.9: 1.82, .38, .50 | -2.0: 1.76, .30, .38 | -3.0: 1.68, .22, .30 | -4.0: 1.58, .15, .22 | -4.6: 1.52, .07, .12. Cowl = z 3.45 to 1.9. Rear fuselage = z 1.9 to -4.6.
- Wing planform (elliptical, semispan 5.62): chord c(x) = 2.5*sqrt(1-(|x|/5.62)^2). The quarter-chord line is the straight line z = 0.30. Leading edge z = 0.30 + 0.25c, trailing edge z = 0.30 - 0.75c. The wing is continuous through the fuselage as one piece from x = -5.62 to +5.62.
- Wing height: dihedral centre line y_c(x) = 1.25 + 0.098*|x|. Thickness t(x) = 0.05 + 0.32*(1-|x|/5.62)^0.8, thickest near 30% chord. Root top is about y 1.41 and root underside about y 1.09. Tip centre is y 1.80.
- Wing hinge line (ailerons and flaps) is at 70% of chord from the leading edge, z = 0.30 - 0.45c. Ailerons run x 2.9 to 5.0, split flaps x 0.75 to 2.8.
- Tail: tailplane centre y = 1.62, z from -3.7 (leading edge at root) to -4.5 (hinge), elevator trailing edge at z = -4.85, half span 1.67, tip rounded. The fin leading edge goes from (y 1.75, z -3.3) up to (y 3.0, z -4.4). The rudder hinge line runs from (y 1.75, z -4.55) up to (y 2.95, z -4.68). The rudder trailing edge is at z = -4.97, with a rounded top at y = 3.0.
- Landing gear: main wheel centres at x = ±1.12, y = 0.34, z = 0.40, tyre radius 0.34, tyre width 0.18. The leg runs from the wing underside at (±1.0, 1.2, 0.35) down to the axle. The tail wheel centre is at (0, 0.14, -4.02), radius 0.14, on a strut from the fuselage belly at (0, 1.38, -3.95).

STYLE (every part): cyanotype blueprint. The aircraft is solid Prussian blue in flat tones. Upward-facing surfaces use skinTop, side and leading-edge surfaces use skinMid, and undersides use skinUnder. Cavities (cockpit, wheel wells, exhaust holes, intakes) are skinDeep. All the drawing is thin white or cyan parts seated 1 to 2 mm proud of the surface: panel-line strips about 6 mm wide, rows of tiny rivet discs (r about 5 mm, 5 to 6 sides) at 8 to 10 cm spacing along seams, wing rib lines, hatch outlines and roundel rings. Draughtsman marks appear too: a dash-dot centreline of short lineCyan dashes along the top of the fuselage and across each wing, and small ruler ticks along the leading-edge spar line. The roundels are concentric flat rings (outer lineWhite, then lineCyan, then lineWhite, centre skinDeep). Faceted low-poly shapes; no gradients, one colour per part.

parts.builds: Merlin cowling and propeller, everything forward of cowlRear (z 1.9). (1) Cowl: loft or lathe through the cowl stations (z 3.45 to 1.9), skinMid with a skinTop upper half. Two long cowl-top bulges (gun troughs) run from z 3.2 to 1.9, with a small raised carburettor-hump panel on top at z 2.4 to 1.9. A skinDeep front opening ring at z 3.45 with an inner rim in lineCyan. (2) Cowl panels: three lineWhite ring seams at z 3.1, 2.6 and 2.2, a horizontal lineWhite seam on each side at engine-centre height, rivet rows along every seam, and four rectangular lineFaint access-hatch outlines per side. (3) Exhausts: six fishtail stacks on each side at x = ±(0.44 to 0.47), y 1.95 to 2.05, z 3.2 to 2.3, spaced evenly. Each is a short skinDeep tapered box with a steelLight collar, and the six stacks sit under a long lineCyan fairing strip. (4) Chin: an under-nose carburettor and oil intake scoop at z 2.2 to 2.9, y about 1.38, a skinUnder box with a skinDeep mouth and a lineWhite frame. (5) Spinner: a pointed cone/lathe from z 3.52 (radius 0.30) to the tip z 4.15 in spinner, with a lineWhite ring seam at z 3.7 and a skinDeep backplate disc of radius 0.34 at z 3.5. (6) Propeller on joint prop: a central hub, three broad blades radiating at 0°, 120° and 240° about the z axis from radius 0.28 to 1.5 (tip y = 3.35). The blades are flat, twisted extrudes, widest about 0.2 at r = 0.7 and tapering to 0.12 at the tip, in skinTop with a lineWhite blade-root band, and the outer 0.18 m of each tip is lineWhite. Each blade has a lineCyan centre-line strip and a small lineCyan stencil mark. Build the propeller and hub on joint prop, everything else on body. Keep clear of the face of the cowl; nothing else sits in front.
parts.attaches: Cowl rear edge meets the fuselage at mount cowlRear (z 1.9, same station: half width .46, half height .48). Propeller and hub are on joint prop at mount propHub.

parts.builds: Fuselage from cowlRear (z 1.9) to the tail cone end (z -4.6), including cockpit and canopy. (1) Main body: one smooth loft through the fuselage stations from z 1.9 to -4.6 (skinTop, skinMid and skinUnder via sectors or bands: skinTop on the upper 70° either side, skinUnder on the belly, skinMid between), with a turtle-deck spine behind the canopy and a dorsal fin fillet blending into the tail part's fin at z -3.3. (2) Canopy on joint canopy: a glass bubble from the windscreen (base mount windscreenBase, z 1.25, y 2.4) rising to apex canopyApex (z -0.1, y 2.62) and ending at canopyRear (z -1.35). Build a sloped front windscreen plus a bullet-proof flat front panel, a sliding hood with three lineWhite frame hoops and two longitudinal rails, and rear fixed glazing. Glass in glass, frames in lineWhite. (3) Cockpit visible through the glass: skinDeep tub floor, a seat at cockpitSeat in skinMid, a headrest armour plate behind the pilot in steelLight, a control column with a spade grip, an instrument panel at z 1.0 with several small lineCyan dial discs and a reflector gunsight (small ring glowing navGlow). (4) Panel lines: lineWhite strips for the cockpit door outline on the left side, circumferential seams at z 0.8, -0.6, -1.5, -2.4, -3.2 and -3.9, a lineWhite stripe running along the mid-height of each side, rivet rows on all seams, and a dash-dot lineCyan centreline along the top. (5) Markings: a roundel on each side at z = -2.4, y about 1.72, outer radius 0.30 (ring lineWhite, lineCyan, lineWhite, centre skinDeep), seated on the curved flank. Two-letter code in lineWhite block strokes (about 0.22 m tall) forward of the roundel on each side at z -1.6, and a small serial number on the rear fuselage. (6) Details: a thin aerial mast on the spine at z 0.6 with a lineWhite wire sweep to the fin, a small lineCyan ID light, a belly skinDeep access hatch outline, and a retracted-tail-wheel doorless slot at the belly z -3.95. Stay clear of the wing: the wing builder owns everything outside the fuselage skin, but the fuselage loft passes straight through the wing root.
parts.attaches: Front at cowlRear; the rear tapers to fuselageTail. Sits over the wing root (wing top y 1.41 at x=0). Fin base at finBase, tailplane roots at tailplaneRootL/R, tail strut at tailStrutTop. Canopy on joint canopy.

parts.builds: Both elliptical wings, built from the shared planform formulas (chord, dihedral, thickness), from x = -5.62 to 5.62 as one continuous airfoil-section solid (loft or extruded planform plus rounded tips). Mid-thickness skinTop on the upper surface, skinMid at the leading edge, skinUnder on the underside. (1) Control surfaces: ailerons (x 2.9 to 5.0) on joints aileronL/aileronR and flaps (x 0.75 to 2.8) on flapL/flapR, trailing-edge strips of 30% chord (hinge at 70% chord), each outlined in lineWhite with 5 to 6 hinge brackets in steelLight, a trim tab on each aileron, and rib stripes in lineFaint across the fabric. Put everything else on body. (2) Surface drawing: spar lines and about 12 rib lines per wing in lineFaint on the upper surface, panel seams for the gun bays in lineWhite, rivet rows along the leading edge, root fillet fairing to the fuselage, a dash-dot lineCyan centre line along the quarter-chord, ruler ticks (tiny lineCyan strips) every 0.25 m along the leading-edge line on the upper surface. (3) Armament: four .303 gun muzzles per wing, short steel tubes projecting 0.10 m from the leading edge at x = 1.9, 2.3, 2.7 and 3.1, each with a skinDeep hole, and ejection slots below, plus two long lineWhite gun-bay hatches on the upper surface and a bulge panel over the ammunition. (4) Radiators: under the left wing an oil cooler at radiatorL and under the right wing a main radiator at radiatorR. Each is a skinUnder box 0.55 wide, 0.35 high and 0.8 long, ducted into the wing underside, with a skinDeep front intake face, a lineCyan honeycomb of 5 to 6 slim strips, and an adjustable flap at the rear. (5) Wheel wells: a skinDeep recess slab on each wing underside at x 0.75 to 1.5, z -0.1 to 0.9, around the leg top (the gear part supplies the doors). (6) Markings: roundels on the upper surface at x = ±3.3 (outer radius 0.40) and on the underside at x = ±3.3, outer radius 0.40, outer ring lineWhite, then lineCyan, lineWhite, centre skinDeep; wing-tip lights as small navGlow lenses at the tips; a pitot tube on the left wing at x = 4.1, protruding forward 0.35 m from the leading edge; a registration cross (two thin crossed lineWhite strips) near each wing tip.
parts.attaches: Passes through the fuselage at wingRootL/wingRootR (centre y 1.25 at x=0). Ailerons are on joints aileronL/aileronR, flaps on flapL/flapR. Leg tops at legTopL/legTopR attach to the underside. Radiators at radiatorL/radiatorR.

parts.builds: The empennage aft of z -3.2, built to the shared tail formulas. (1) Fin: a swept, thin extruded plate (thickness 0.08 to 0.04) with its leading edge going from (y 1.75, z -3.3) to (y 3.0, z -4.4), merging at the base into the fuselage fillet, in skinTop with a skinMid leading-edge strip. (2) Rudder on joint rudder: the trailing portion behind the hinge line, ending at z -4.97 with a rounded top at y 3.0, ribbed with 8 lineFaint horizontal rib stripes, a trim tab at the bottom, hinge brackets, and a navGlow tail light at the trailing tip. Rudder and tab are separate parts on joint rudder. (3) Tailplanes: left and right flat extruded planforms, half span 1.67 with rounded tips, root chord from z -3.7 to the hinge at -4.5, thickness 0.08 at the root tapering to 0.03, in skinTop with skinUnder undersides and root fillets. (4) Elevators on joints elevatorL/elevatorR: the rear section from hinge z -4.5 to the trailing edge z -4.85, with horn balances at the tips, lineFaint rib stripes, small trim tabs, and hinge brackets in steelLight. (5) Markings: a fin flash on the front of the fin, three vertical stripes in lineWhite, lineCyan and lineFaint (fin-flash replaced by blueprint line colours), 0.5 m tall and 0.1 m wide, seated on the fin surface, plus a lineWhite outline around the fin and tailplane silhouettes, rib lines on the tailplanes, rivet rows along the fin leading edge and tailplane leading edges, a dash-dot lineCyan centre line along the fin, a small registration cross at the fin tip, and bracing struts under the tailplane in steel (short boxes from the fuselage at x ±0.2).
parts.attaches: Fin base at finBase on the fuselage fillet, tailplane roots at tailplaneRootL/R, hinges at elevatorHingeL/R and rudderHingeBase; the rudder top is rudderTop.

parts.builds: Undercarriage: two main legs and the tail wheel. (1) Main legs on joints legL/legR: a steel oleo strut running from legTopL/R (1.0, 1.2, 0.35) to the axle at axleL/R (1.12, 0.34, 0.4), with a thicker upper cylinder in steel and a slimmer lower piston in steelLight, a torque-link scissor pair, a brake line (thin lineCyan sweep), and an axle stub. (2) Wheels on joints wheelL/wheelR: radius 0.34, width 0.18. Tyre in inkNavy with a tread ring of 16 small facets, a lineFaint sidewall ring, a spinner-coloured hub disc with 5 round lightening holes in skinDeep, a lineWhite rim ring, and 6 hub rivets. Wheels are faceted (16 to 20 sides). (3) Leg fairing doors: a large flat door plate on each outer side of the leg, hinged at the wing underside, height 0.7, in skinMid with lineWhite outline, rivet row and lineCyan hinge strips, plus a small inner door plate beside the well. (4) Tail gear on joints tailLeg/tailWheel: a short oleo strut from tailStrutTop (0, 1.38, -3.95) down to the axle at tailWheelAxle (0, 0.14, -4.02), with a fork, and a small faceted tail wheel of radius 0.14 and width 0.09 (inkNavy tyre, spinner hub) resting on y = 0. (5) The lowest points of both main tyres and the tail tyre rest on y = 0. Also add a lineCyan 'ground contact' tick mark on each tyre and ruler marks on the oleo, as drafting annotation.
parts.attaches: Main leg tops at legTopL/legTopR against the wing underside (recess built by wings), axles at axleL/axleR. Tail strut top at tailStrutTop under the fuselage belly.

calls.reasoning:
I'm settling on a spec for a Spitfire in cyanotype blueprint style and deciding whether it should be static or have joints. A propeller joint and control surfaces seem worth including, though I want to keep the joints modest. I'm also pulling the Mk I dimensions, roughly 11.23 m wingspan and 9.12 m length, and planning to work at real scale while the plane stands on its landing gear.

I'm working out the Spitfire's proportions at real scale, with the wheels on the ground and the propeller tip reaching roughly 3 m, so the bounding box comes to about 11.2 by 3.0 by 9.1 m. For the look, I'm leaning toward a Prussian blue palette with white linework for panel lines, rivets, and roundels, and I'm thinking about a few drafted edge strips and rib lines on the wings.

I'm checking the vertical numbers now: with the prop radius at about 1.5 m and the shaft near 1.85 m, the top of the propeller lands around 3.35 m, so I'm setting the height to 3.4 m. That leaves the prop bottom just above the ground, which is close to real clearance.

I'm fixing the nose tip at z≈4.15 and the rudder's trailing edge at z≈-4.95 to match the 9.1 m length. Next I'm splitting the work between builders: one takes the nose, prop, and engine details, and another takes the wings with their ailerons, flaps, gun ports, and the radiators underneath.

I'm splitting the rest of the design into five parts: nose, fuselage, wings, tail, and gear, with a rough budget of about 900 across them. The wings look like the heaviest share, so I'm giving them the largest allotment.

I'm assigning joint names and hinge placements for the propeller, rudder, elevators, ailerons, gear legs, wheels, tail wheel, and canopy, with the rudder hinge set near the tail and the elevator and aileron hinges running along their axes.

I'm working out the wing geometry now: an elliptical planform with roughly a 2.4 m root chord and a 5.6 m semispan, with a slight dihedral and the wing root sitting low on the fuselage at about y≈1.3 m.

I'm settling the wing geometry: the root sits near y≈1.3 with a slight dihedral, so the tips rise to about 1.85. For the main gear, I'm placing the wheels at roughly x≈±1.05 with a radius near 0.34, and the legs run from the wing underside outward to the axles.

I'm weighing how to place the gear legs relative to the wing: the wheels sit around x≈±1.0 with the leg tops slightly inboard, and the wing underside rises a little as it moves outward under the dihedral.

I'm placing the main gear legs at the wing underside, with each wheel axle around x≈±1.1 and z≈0.4. For the tail wheel, I'm checking how far its strut has to drop from the rear fuselage at z≈-3.9 down to a small wheel near the ground.

I'm weighing the tail wheel strut against a tilted fuselage, since a tail-down attitude would shorten it. Keeping the level pose is simpler, so I'm considering sloping the rear fuselage instead, with the centerline dropping from about y≈1.85 at the nose to about y≈1.55 near z≈-4.6.

I'm weighing whether to tilt the airframe so the tail wheel strut can stay short, or to keep the level pose and accept a tall oleo strut with a fairing. The tilt would add complexity for all five builders, so I'm leaning toward the simpler tall strut.

I'm sketching the fuselage's shape now, with the nose cowl about 0.5 m in radius and the cockpit near 0.85 m wide, and I'm setting the tail wheel's strut to run from about 1.42 m down to 0.28 m.

I'm sizing the fuselage stations now: the front cowl ring sits near z≈3.5 with a radius around 0.4, and the spinner base is a bit smaller, around 0.3, at z≈3.52. I'm also weighing how far the cowl runs back before the nose section meets the cockpit, roughly 2.1 to 2.2 m from the prop plane.

I'm setting the fuselage stations next: the cowl tapers from about 0.4 to 0.48 m in radius between z≈3.45 and 1.9, then the windscreen starts at z≈1.3 and the canopy runs back to z≈-0.9 with its top near y≈2.58. Behind that the rear fuselage narrows to a tail end of about 0.1 m radius at z≈-4.7. For the fin, I'm sizing the rudder from z≈-4.0 to -4.95 and running its height up toward 3.35 m.

I'm settling the tail dimensions now: the tailplane spans about 3.35 m with its chord running from roughly z -3.7 to -4.5, and the elevator hinge sits near z -4.4. The rudder's trailing edge goes to about z -4.95, a little past the elevator's edge at -4.85.

I'm working out the wing's planform now, using an elliptical chord distribution with the quarter-chord line held near z≈0.3, which puts the root leading edge around z≈0.9 and the trailing edge near -1.6. I'm still deciding how to round off the tip chord.

I'm setting the wing's thickness at about 0.32 m at the root, thinning to 0.08 m at the tip, and tilting the span up with roughly 6° of dihedral so the wing root sits near y≈1.25 and the tips reach about 1.8.

I'm settling the wing-to-gear placement: the leg runs from the wing underside down to the axle, which will be stubbier than I first assumed, with the wheel sitting about 0.7 m off the ground. Next I need a precise wing planform formula so the tail and fuselage can match, with ailerons outboard, flaps inboard, and the radiators tucked under the wings around x≈±1.8 to ±2.7.

I'm settling the radiator boxes at about 0.55 by 0.35 by 0.8 m, tucked under the wings near z≈-0.2 with their bottoms around y≈1.0. Next I'm planning the gun barrels, eight .303s with four small stubs projecting from each wing's leading edge at x≈2.0 to 3.5, and I'm fixing the wing root mount point at [0.45, 1.25, -0.3].

Now I'm picking the colour palette for the blueprint: deep Prussian blue for the main skin, lighter and darker blues for the upper and lower surfaces, and white for the line work, with a soft cyan for the canopy glass and gun steel.

I'm settling the colour palette for the blueprint now: a Prussian blue base with white for the panel seams, roundels in concentric white, light blue, and dark blue rings, and dash-dot centerlines along the fuselage top. I'm also planning to give every panel seam its own thin line-colour strip, with wing rib lines drawn in the same way.

I'm listing the mount points next: the prop hub at the nose, the cowl's rear edge, the windscreen base, the canopy's rear, and the tail end of the fuselage. For the left tailplane root I'm working out the fuselage centerline height at that station, which drops from about 1.82 near the canopy back to roughly 1.52 at the tail.

I'm fixing the tailplane root at y≈1.62 with a thin profile, since the fuselage there is only about 0.4 m tall. Next I'm sketching the fin's planform, with its leading edge running from z≈-3.6 at the base up to the top near y≈3.0, and the rudder hinge angling back from the base to the top.

I'm listing the joint definitions now, starting with the body root along the spine and the propeller hinge at the nose. I'm also placing the canopy slider, which I'm still weighing as an extra joint for the fuselage builder.

I'm placing the aileron hinge along the outer wing, working out where the line falls on the chord at about x≈3.0 so the control surface matches the wing planform.

I'm working out the aileron hinge at the outer wing, placing it around x≈3.0 and z≈-0.65 so it falls about 70% back along the chord. At x≈5.0 the hinge comes out near z≈-0.21, so the line runs outward and slightly forward, and I'm settling its direction from there.

I'm checking the aileron hinge direction, which tilts outward and slightly forward, and then I'm placing the elevator hinges at the tailplane roots, one on each side with opposite directions.

I'm placing the rudder hinge on the fin near the tail, raked slightly back as it rises, and then setting the left leg from the wing underside down toward the wheel. The tail wheel strut runs from the rear fuselage underside straight down, with its wheel hinge at the bottom.

I'm working out the gear leg splay now: the top sits at about x 1.0, y 1.2, and the axle lands near x 1.12, y 0.34, with the wing's underside around y 1.35 at that station.

I'm setting the bounding boxes for the parts now, with the nose box spanning about 3 m wide and reaching up to the propeller tip, and I'm leaving the floor off since the nose has none.

Still working through the nose details: the spinner and three-bladed prop, with white tips, then the cowl panels, six fishtail exhaust stacks on each side, and the gun-trough humps on top.

I'm laying out the fuselage part now, with its box spanning the main body from the cowl's rear edge back toward the tail, and I'm listing the details it has to carry: the canopy and windscreen, the cockpit interior, panel lines, and roundels on each side.

I'm moving on to the fuselage details: the fuselage at this station is about 0.6 m tall, so I'm using a radius near 0.3 for the cross-section, with code letters, the aerial mast, and the dorsal centreline still on the list. I'm also checking whether the wing should run continuously through the centre section from one tip to the other, or be built as two halves starting at the centreline.

I'm settling the wing root so it starts at the centreline and runs under the fuselage, with the fuselage bottom sitting just above it. The fuselage's lower bound at the wing stays around y≈1.25, and I'm adding root fillets on the wing builder's side, with the fuselage body widening near z≈0.3.

I'm working through the fuselage cross-sections now, setting a centre height near y≈1.85 and tracking the half-width and half-height at each station as the body runs back from the cowl: wider and taller near the wing, then narrowing toward the tail.

I'm fixing the fuselage's upper profile around the canopy and tail: the canopy apex sits near 2.62 m, the windscreen frame tops out near 2.55 m, and the turtle deck drops to about 2.26 m at the rear. The fuselage's floor width comes to roughly 0.43 m half-width.

I'm checking the cowl stations against the fuselage width at that point, which holds the front ring near 0.4 to 0.47 in radius. Then I'm turning to the tail part, sizing its box to take in the fin, rudder, tailplanes, and elevators.

I'm defining the tail part's box so it covers the fin, rudder, tailplanes, and elevators, with a red-white-blue fin flash along the leading edge and nothing under the tail cone. Then I'm sizing the wings part to span the full wingspan, down to the radiators and back to the ailerons and flaps.

I'm now defining the gear part's bounding box, and I'm noting that the wing builder will own the wheel-well recess slab on the underside while the gear builder takes the leg, fork, wheel, doors, and tail gear.

I'm pinning down the gear part's bounding box at x [-1.3, 1.3], y [0, 1.4], z [-4.2, 0.8]. The wheels touch the ground, so the floor is set on for this part. Since the total length runs from -4.97 to 4.15, the overall size works out to about 11.25 by 3.35 by 9.12 m.

Checking the vertical clearance next: the propeller's lowest point sits around 0.35 m, well above the ground and far ahead of the wheels, so the nose prop has no conflict with the gear. I'm also settling on a blueprint style, with raised white panel strips and ruler-like tick marks along the wing edges and a registration mark on the tail.

I'm listing the colour palette for the blueprint now: a Prussian blue base with a few shades for the top, middle, and underside surfaces, a deep navy for the cockpit, wells, and shadows, and white and pale cyan for the line work and canopy glass.

I'm listing the remaining colours for the blueprint: a steel blue for the guns and legs, a lighter steel for highlights, and a pale spinner tone for the hubs. The roundels will use white, cyan, and deep-blue rings, with navy for the cockpit and nav-light glow. Next I'm placing the mount points and the joint definitions.

I'm now writing the wing geometry as a formula: the centreline height rises with distance from the fuselage, from about 1.25 at the root to roughly 1.8 at the tips, and the wing thickness tapers outward. I'm planning to loft the wing from span stations so the builder can follow the same shape.

I'm settling how the wing gets built: any approach works, as long as the outer silhouette matches the planform. The ailerons run from about x≈2.9 to 5.0, with the flaps inboard from x≈0.75 to 2.8. I'm also working out the part budgets, roughly 850 in total, and placing the wing roundels on top at x≈±3.3.

Next I'm estimating the wing's top-surface roundel at x≈3.3, where the chord and thickness give a surface height around 1.68, and I'm writing the wings builder to compute that from its own wing surface. The fuselage roundels will go on each side at z≈-2.4.

I'm sketching out buildNose with a budget of 170 parts, placing the nose along the +Z axis at y=1.85. I've worked out the cowl width and height at four stations along the length, and I'm starting to build the cowl as a loft through those stations.

Still writing the cowl loft and figuring out how to find its surface for the seam rings...

Rivets are the awkward part: placing a small sphere at each point along the loop means one part per rivet, and three rings of about 36 each would blow the 170-part budget. I'm thinking of merging all the rivet geometries into a single part instead, and I still need to check that a sphere placed with `at` will orient correctly.

Still working through the rivet placement: merging them into one geometry, pulling their positions from the loop path, and nudging them outward so they sit on the surface. I'm also planning three seam sweeps at the ring stations, and considering a horizontal seam at the cowl's midline.

Still working out the side seams: I'm going to get them from surface ray hits at angle 90° rather than an ellipse formula, with a small outward lift so they sit proud of the cowl.

Still building the closed ring of 28 surface points, with rivets at every other point, and I'm planning eight thin rectangular hatch outlines on the sides, placed between the seam rings.

Still working out the hatch panels and the two gun troughs on top of the cowl, sampling the cowl surface at x = ±0.15 to get the trough height.
